column4: Summary
column5: Description

column4: Platform and delivery pipeline
column5: Azure environments, CI/CD, and operational basics for dev, test, and production.

column4: Identity, access, and consent
column5: Entra sign-in, role and care-relationship checks, consent, emergency access, and audit.

column4: Clinical integration
column5: HL7 and FHIR feeds, patient matching, terminology, and message operations.

column4: Patient record and care coordination
column5: Patient record, worklist, tasks, and discharge follow-up.

column4: Referral management
column5: Referral intake, triage, booking, and service matching.

column4: AI discharge drafting
column5: Cited draft summaries that a clinician must review and sign.

column4: Clinical safety, privacy, and compliance
column5: Safety case, privacy impact assessment, regulatory classification, and approvals.

column4: Security and network hardening
column5: Front Door and WAF, network design, database roles, audit export, and penetration testing.

column4: Testing and quality
column5: Test strategy, SIT, UAT, performance, and accessibility.

column4: Operations and support
column5: Monitoring, ServiceNow incidents, runbooks, and service handover.

column4: Change, training, and pilot rollout
column5: Operating model, SOPs, training, and the pilot ward.

column4: Data platform and analytics
column5: De-identified analytics zone, reporting, and KPIs. Phase 4 of the design.

column4: Risk models and MLOps
column5: Readmission and capacity models with clinical governance. Phase 4 and 5 of the design.

column4: FHIR store and clinical feeds
column5: Azure Health Data Services FHIR store, and pathology, imaging, GP, pharmacy, and rostering feeds. Phase 2 of the design.

column4: Patient identity and terminology
column5: Matching beyond exact MRN, national identifiers, and clinical terminology mapping. Phase 2 of the design.

column4: Referral service matching
column5: Service catalogue, eligibility rules, wait times, and status updates for referrers. Phase 3 of the design.

column4: Patient reminders
column5: SMS appointment reminders and contact preferences. Phase 3 of the design.

column4: Language-model drafting
column5: Discharge drafts and referral extraction with a language model, after safety approval. Phase 5 of the design.

column4: Hospital-wide rollout and partners
column5: Scale from the pilot ward to the hospital, then GP and community partners. Phase 6 of the design.

column4: Production scale and resilience
column5: Second-region recovery, scale testing, and cost control for full production. Phase 6 of the design.

column4: Build the API, portal, Terraform, and pipelines for the first release
column5:
First release code is in the repository: Spring Boot API, Angular portal, Terraform, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions pipelines.

Acceptance criteria:
* Backend and frontend tests pass locally
* Terraform validates
* Pipeline YAML parses

column4: Choose GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps, and delete the other
column5:
Both pipeline sets deploy to the same environments and cannot see each other's locks, so only one can stay.

Acceptance criteria:
* Decision recorded with reason
* Unused pipeline folder deleted
* README updated

column4: Run the Azure bootstrap script and create the state storage and registry
column5:
Run infra/bootstrap.sh in the chosen subscription, in an Australian region.

Acceptance criteria:
* State storage and registry exist
* Values recorded as pipeline variables
* No admin user on the registry

column4: Set up pipeline identity, environments, and approvals
column5:
Create the federated identity, environments, variables, and production approvers as the README describes. Hand over to Sreehari after the first deployment.

Acceptance criteria:
* Federated sign-in works with no stored secrets
* Production needs a named approver
* Deployments are limited to main

column4: First deployment to dev, and fix what the first pipeline run finds
column5:
The Dockerfiles, nginx setup, pipelines, and Azure SQL connection have never run. Expect fixes.

Acceptance criteria:
* Images build in the registry
* Both apps healthy in dev
* Portal reachable from allowed networks only
* Flyway migrations ran on Azure SQL

column4: Run the backend test suite against SQL Server in CI
column5:
Local tests used H2. The CI job against SQL Server has never run.

Acceptance criteria:
* CI job passes on SQL Server
* Any SQL dialect issues fixed in the migrations

column4: Deploy the test environment
column5:
Promote the dev images to test using the pipeline.

Acceptance criteria:
* Same image tag runs in dev and test
* Test uses masked or synthetic data only

column4: Narrow pipeline permissions from subscription-wide roles
column5:
The pipeline identity holds Contributor and User Access Administrator on the whole subscription.

Owner: Security Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Roles scoped to the CareConnect resource groups
* Role assignment limited to AcrPull for the app identity

column4: Role, care-relationship, and consent checks on every patient read
column5:
AccessService allows a read only with a care relationship and active care consent, or a current emergency grant.

Acceptance criteria:
* Denied reads return 403 and are audited
* Consent withdrawal blocks the next read

column4: Emergency access with a required reason
column5:
Clinicians can open a record in an emergency for 4 hours after giving a reason.

Acceptance criteria:
* Reason of at least 10 characters
* Grant is audited for privacy review

column4: Create the Entra app registrations and app roles
column5:
Create the API and portal registrations, the access_as_user scope, and the five app roles.

Acceptance criteria:
* Version 2 access tokens
* Test users assigned for each role
* Portal redirect URI added after first deployment

column4: Load care-team membership from the EMR or rostering system
column5:
Nothing fills care_team_member, so staff cannot open records through normal access. This blocks every clinical test.

Acceptance criteria:
* Source and refresh frequency agreed
* Members added and removed automatically
* Changes audited

column4: Privacy officer screen for emergency access review
column5:
The API records emergency grants, but there is no review screen.

Acceptance criteria:
* List of unreviewed grants with reason and user
* Reviewer records an outcome and comment
* Overdue reviews are highlighted

column4: Privacy officer screen for patient audit trails
column5:
Show the existing /patients/{id}/audit API in the portal.

Acceptance criteria:
* Filter by user, action, and date
* Viewing an audit trail is itself audited

column4: Confirm consent rules for each use of patient data
column5:
The design assumes care sharing is permitted by policy and research needs opt-in. Legal and privacy must confirm.

Owner: Privacy Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Written rules for care, research, and GP sharing
* Code changes raised for any difference

column4: Receive HL7 admission and discharge messages
column5:
ADT A01 and A03 over HTTPS, with raw message storage, duplicate detection, and a follow-up task on discharge.

Acceptance criteria:
* Duplicates acknowledged without reprocessing
* Failed messages stored as FAILED

column4: Agree EMR test feed access and message samples
column5:
The EMR vendor must provide a test feed, message specifications, and synthetic samples.

Acceptance criteria:
* Contact and timeline agreed with the vendor
* Specification and 50 synthetic samples received

column4: Alert on failed HL7 messages
column5:
Failed messages are stored, but nobody is told.

Acceptance criteria:
* ServiceNow incident within 5 minutes of a failure
* Incident has the control ID and no patient data

column4: Reprocess failed HL7 messages
column5:
Operators need to replay a stored message after a mapping fix.

Acceptance criteria:
* Integration role can replay by control ID
* Replay is audited and idempotent

column4: Confirm the site time zone for HL7 times
column5:
Times without a zone are treated as UTC, which would shift Australian times.

Acceptance criteria:
* Zone confirmed with hospital IT
* Code updated and tested with daylight saving dates

column4: HL7 conformance tests with real message samples
column5:
Test against the vendor's synthetic samples, including unusual and malformed messages.

Acceptance criteria:
* All sample types processed or rejected correctly
* Results report shared with the vendor

column4: Worklist, patient record, and task completion
column5:
Worklist for the care team, patient record with encounters, notes, tasks, and care team.

Acceptance criteria:
* Only care-team patients are shown

column4: Usability test the worklist and patient record with coordinators
column5:
Test with at least five coordinators and nurses, using synthetic data in dev.

Acceptance criteria:
* Findings ranked by severity
* Changes raised as stories

column4: Create and assign tasks from the patient record
column5:
The API supports creating tasks, but the portal does not.

Acceptance criteria:
* Task title, due date, and assignee
* Validation messages are clear

column4: Accessibility review against WCAG 2.2 AA
column5:
Automated and manual review of all portal screens.

Acceptance criteria:
* No serious axe issues
* Keyboard-only walkthrough passes

column4: Referral triage and booking
column5:
Triage clinicians set urgency with a reason, then book.

Acceptance criteria:
* Booking requires triage first

column4: Create referrals from the portal
column5:
The API supports creating referrals, but the portal does not.

Acceptance criteria:
* Service and reason required

column4: Cited discharge drafts that need a clinician's signature
column5:
Drafts quote source notes, flag unsupported numbers, and file nothing until signed. Off by default in deployed environments.

Acceptance criteria:
* Unsigned drafts are not part of the record
* Kill switch tested

column4: Clinical review of the draft review screen and wording
column5:
Confirm the labels, warnings, and signing step meet clinical expectations.

Owner: Clinical Lead (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Clinical lead sign-off recorded

column4: Appoint the Clinical Safety Officer and Privacy Officer
column5:
Both roles must be in place before design approval and any shared testing.

Acceptance criteria:
* Named people with agreed time commitment

column4: Clinical safety case and hazard log
column5:
Record hazards such as wrong-patient display, failed messages, and AI errors, with controls.

Owner: Clinical Safety Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Hazard log reviewed by the clinical lead
* Safety case approved before pilot

column4: Privacy impact assessment
column5:
Assess data flows, consent, emergency access, retention, and AI processing.

Owner: Privacy Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Actions tracked as Jira issues
* Approved before pilot

column4: Regulatory classification of each AI feature
column5:
Get specialist advice on whether any feature counts as a medical device under TGA rules.

Owner: Clinical Safety Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Written classification for each feature

column4: Confirm health record retention rules by state
column5:
Includes longer periods for children's records.

Owner: Privacy Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Retention rules documented and applied in design

column4: Add Front Door and WAF in place of IP allow-listing
column5:
The portal is currently reachable only from allow-listed networks.

Acceptance criteria:
* WAF in prevention mode
* Container app reachable only through Front Door

column4: Separate database roles for migrations and the app
column5:
The app identity is the SQL administrator, so a compromised app could alter the audit table and its trigger.

Acceptance criteria:
* App runs with read and write only
* Migrations use a separate identity
* Audit table cannot be changed by the app

column4: Export the audit log to immutable storage and Sentinel
column5:
Audit records must survive a database compromise.

Owner: Security Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Export within 15 minutes
* Alerts on unusual access patterns

column4: Hospital network connectivity design
column5:
Design the hub network and private connection to the hospital for HL7 and staff access.

Acceptance criteria:
* Design approved by hospital network team
* Address ranges agreed

column4: Independent penetration test
column5:
Book an external tester, including AI-specific tests.

Owner: Security Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* No open critical or high findings at pilot

column4: Disaster recovery design and rehearsal
column5:
Meet a 5-minute recovery point and 1-hour recovery time.

Acceptance criteria:
* Rehearsal completed and results recorded

column4: Test plan for the pilot release
column5:
Cover functional, access, consent, HL7, AI drafting, and downtime scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
* Plan reviewed by clinical lead and tech lead

column4: Clinical safety test scenarios
column5:
Wrong-patient, failed message, withdrawn consent, and AI warning scenarios from the hazard log.

Acceptance criteria:
* Each hazard has a linked test

column4: System integration testing with the EMR test feed
column5:
End-to-end tests from EMR message to worklist.

Acceptance criteria:
* All critical scenarios pass
* Defects triaged daily

column4: Performance test at peak message and user volume
column5:
1 million messages a day and 500 concurrent users, from the design targets.

Acceptance criteria:
* 95% of record loads under 2 seconds

column4: User acceptance testing with the pilot ward
column5:
Scenarios run by coordinators, nurses, and clinicians.

Acceptance criteria:
* Signed UAT acceptance

column4: ServiceNow incidents from Azure Monitor alerts
column5:
Route app health, failed deployments, and HL7 failures to the right support group.

Acceptance criteria:
* Priority set by severity
* No patient data in incidents

column4: Monitoring dashboard and alert rules
column5:
Service health, HL7 backlog, failed messages, and emergency access counts.

Acceptance criteria:
* Shared with operations and on-call

column4: Runbooks for on-call support
column5:
Failed deployment, HL7 failure, AI kill switch, and access complaints.

Acceptance criteria:
* Reviewed in a tabletop exercise

column4: Current-state review of discharge and referral processes
column5:
Map how wards work today, to plan the pilot and training.

Acceptance criteria:
* Process maps reviewed by the pilot ward

column4: Choose the pilot ward and clinical champions
column5:
Work with the clinical lead and nursing management.

Acceptance criteria:
* Ward and champions named

column4: SOPs and training material for the pilot
column5:
Include downtime procedures and how to report a safety concern.

Acceptance criteria:
* Training delivered to all pilot staff

column4: Release and cutover plan for the pilot
column5:
Go and no-go criteria, rollback, communications, and hypercare roster.

Acceptance criteria:
* Go and no-go meeting held

column4: Pilot success measures and baseline
column5:
Follow-up within 7 days, referral wait, and documentation time.

Acceptance criteria:
* Baseline measured before go-live

column4: Provision the FHIR store with AU Base profiles
column5:
Deploy Azure Health Data Services FHIR R4 in Terraform, with private access only and FHIR AU Base profiles loaded.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Created by Terraform in dev and test
* No public network access
* Profile validation enabled

column4: Convert admissions and discharges into FHIR
column5:
Map ADT messages to Patient, Encounter, and Provenance resources, keeping the raw message for reprocessing.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Mapping reviewed by the clinical lead
* Round-trip tests with vendor samples
* Provenance links each resource to its message

column4: Receive pathology results
column5:
HL7 v2 ORU results stored as FHIR Observation, with LOINC codes and units.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Abnormal flags preserved
* Unknown codes kept and reported, not dropped
* Results appear on the patient timeline

column4: Receive imaging reports
column5:
Report text only, as FHIR DiagnosticReport. Images stay in the imaging system.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Report linked to its encounter
* Amended reports replace earlier versions with history

column4: Receive GP referral letters
column5:
Secure messaging or PDF letters, with Document Intelligence extracting the referral fields for a person to confirm.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Original letter stored and viewable
* Extracted fields need confirmation before triage
* Unreadable letters routed to a work queue

column4: Receive discharge medicines from pharmacy
column5:
FHIR MedicationRequest with AMT codes, shown on the patient record.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Changed and stopped medicines are clearly marked
* Pharmacist review status shown

column4: Load rosters and shifts for staffing forecasts
column5:
Daily load from the rostering system through Data Factory.

Acceptance criteria:
* Loads reconcile to rostering totals
* Leave reasons are not loaded

column4: FHIR conformance testing
column5:
Validate stored resources against AU Base profiles with the Inferno and HAPI validators.

Acceptance criteria:
* No profile errors for supported resources
* Results report attached

column4: Look up national healthcare identifiers
column5:
Use the Healthcare Identifiers Service to find each patient's IHI. Needs registration and conformance testing with the service operator.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Registration and conformance complete
* Lookups audited
* Unverified identifiers are marked

column4: Match patients by identifier and demographics
column5:
Link records automatically only on high-confidence matches. A wrong merge is a patient safety incident.

Acceptance criteria:
* Matching rules approved by the clinical safety officer
* Uncertain matches go to a steward
* Accuracy measured on a labelled test set

column4: Data steward screen for uncertain matches
column5:
Compare two records side by side and decide whether to link them.

Acceptance criteria:
* Decision needs a reason
* Every decision audited

column4: Unlink records that were wrongly merged
column5:
Reverse a link, and move each piece of data back to the right patient.

Acceptance criteria:
* Unlinking is reversible and audited
* Affected clinicians are notified

column4: Map clinical codes to national terminologies
column5:
Map local codes to SNOMED CT-AU, LOINC, AMT, and ICD-10-AM, using a terminology service.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Mapping coverage report by source
* Unmapped codes kept and reported

column4: Service catalogue with eligibility rules
column5:
Services, eligibility criteria, locations, and owners, maintained by referral managers.

Acceptance criteria:
* Rule changes need approval
* Catalogue changes are versioned

column4: Suggest services during triage
column5:
Rank eligible services by urgency, next available slot, and distance. The clinician always decides.

Acceptance criteria:
* Each suggestion shows why it is eligible
* Clinician's choice and any override reason recorded

column4: Load wait times and next available slots
column5:
Daily wait-time data from outpatient scheduling.

Acceptance criteria:
* Freshness shown on screen
* Stale data flagged

column4: Send referral status updates to the referring GP
column5:
Tell the GP when a referral is received, triaged, and booked.

Owner: HL7 and FHIR Integration Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Sent through secure messaging
* Failures retried and reported

column4: Send SMS appointment reminders
column5:
Reminders through Azure Communication Services, with no clinical details in the message.

Acceptance criteria:
* Only patients who agreed receive messages
* Delivery status recorded
* Opt-out by reply works

column4: Record contact preferences and interpreter needs
column5:
Preferred contact method, language, and interpreter needs, shown on the record.

Acceptance criteria:
* Changes audited
* Preferences respected by the reminder service

column4: Privacy review of patient messaging
column5:
Confirm consent, content, and retention for SMS.

Owner: Privacy Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Written approval before the first message is sent

column4: Isolated analytics zone in Azure
column5:
Separate network, ADLS Gen2, Databricks, and Unity Catalog, with no route to the clinical zone except approved exports.

Acceptance criteria:
* Created by Terraform
* No public endpoints
* Access reviewed by security

column4: De-identification service
column5:
Remove direct identifiers, replace patient keys with a keyed token, shift dates, and suppress small groups.

Acceptance criteria:
* Privacy officer approves the method
* Re-identification test by an independent reviewer
* Free text excluded by default

column4: Bulk FHIR export into Bronze
column5:
Scheduled export from the FHIR store through the de-identification service.

Acceptance criteria:
* Daily export completes within its window
* Row counts reconcile to the FHIR store

column4: Silver and Gold models for encounters, referrals, and beds
column5:
Build the reporting model from the design: encounters, referrals, bed occupancy, follow-ups, and AI outputs.

Acceptance criteria:
* Definitions agreed with clinical leads
* Data quality checks on every load

column4: Data quality and equity checks
column5:
Completeness, timeliness, validity, and missing-data rates by patient group.

Acceptance criteria:
* Failures raise alerts
* Equity report shared with model governance

column4: Register datasets in Purview with lineage
column5:
Owners, classifications, and lineage for every analytics dataset.

Acceptance criteria:
* Every Gold dataset has an owner

column4: Operational reports in Power BI
column5:
Follow-up within 7 days, referral waits, discharge timeliness, and emergency access trends.

Acceptance criteria:
* Row-level security by service
* Figures match source systems

column4: Ethics and governance approval for model development
column5:
Confirm whether ethics approval is needed, and agree the intended use of each model.

Owner: Clinical Safety Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Written decision for each model

column4: MLOps pipeline with MLflow and Unity Catalog
column5:
Training jobs, experiment tracking, signed model registry, and Databricks Asset Bundles deployed from Git.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Every model traceable to its data and code
* Promotion needs an approval record

column4: Readmission risk model
column5:
Calibrated gradient boosting, trained on de-identified data. Used to offer extra support, never to reduce care.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* AUROC at least 0.72 and calibration error at most 0.05 on held-out data
* Results reported by patient group

column4: Missed-appointment risk model
column5:
Used only to offer reminders and support. It must not be used for overbooking or lowering priority.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Use restriction written into the model card
* Results reported by patient group

column4: Bed and staffing forecasts
column5:
Seven-day ward forecasts with an 80% range.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Accuracy measured against actuals
* Range shown on every forecast

column4: Eight-week silent trial of risk models
column5:
Score live patients without showing the results to care teams.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Silent trial report reviewed by the safety committee

column4: Show risk levels and reasons on worklists
column5:
Low, medium, or high with the main factors, and a way to dismiss with a reason.

Acceptance criteria:
* Labelled as decision support
* Dismissals recorded for monitoring

column4: Model governance screen
column5:
Performance by patient group, clinician feedback, drift, and approval evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
* Matches the design's governance screen
* Read-only for most users

column4: Model monitoring and per-ward kill switch
column5:
Alert on drift and performance drops, and turn off any model for any ward without a release.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Kill switch tested in each environment
* Alerts routed to ServiceNow

column4: Clinician-reviewed evaluation set for discharge drafts
column5:
Synthetic and de-identified cases with reference summaries, reviewed by clinicians.

Owner: Clinical Lead (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* At least 200 cases
* Covers medicines, allergies, and follow-up

column4: Deploy a private language model in an Australian region
column5:
Azure OpenAI with private access, managed identity, and contract terms that bar training on patient data.

Acceptance criteria:
* No public endpoint
* Data stays in Australian regions

column4: Automated evaluation in the pipeline
column5:
Score omissions, unsupported statements, and medicine errors on every prompt or model change.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* No critical medicine errors
* Unsupported statements under 1%
* Release blocked on failure

column4: Prompt injection and data leakage testing
column5:
Test notes that contain instructions, and attempts to reach another patient's data.

Owner: Security Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* No successful injections in the test set

column4: Extract referral details from GP letters with a language model
column5:
Suggestions only, for a triage clinician to confirm.

Owner: ML Engineer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Each extracted field links to its source text

column4: Safety approval and ward-by-ward enablement
column5:
Enable the language model one ward at a time after approval.

Owner: Clinical Safety Officer (not yet in the team).

Acceptance criteria:
* Approval recorded before each ward goes live

column4: Pilot benefits and safety review
column5:
Compare pilot results with the baseline, and review every safety concern raised.

Acceptance criteria:
* Report presented to the sponsor and safety committee

column4: Rollout plan for remaining wards
column5:
Order wards by readiness, with training, champions, and hypercare for each wave.

Acceptance criteria:
* Plan approved by nursing and medical leads

column4: Training and champions for each rollout wave
column5:
Train staff and champions before each wave goes live.

Acceptance criteria:
* Every user trained before access
* Feedback collected after each wave

column4: Secure access for GP and community partners
column5:
Partner staff see referral status and signed discharge information only, through External ID.

Acceptance criteria:
* Access limited to their patients
* Partner agreement signed before access

column4: Data sharing agreements with partners
column5:
Agreements covering purpose, access, retention, and breach response.

Acceptance criteria:
* Reviewed by legal and the privacy officer

column4: Hand over to business-as-usual support
column5:
ServiceNow support groups, knowledge articles, and service levels.

Acceptance criteria:
* Support team signs off the handover

column4: Second-region recovery for the clinical zone
column5:
Recovery in Australia Southeast for the database, FHIR store, and apps.

Acceptance criteria:
* Failover rehearsed twice a year
* Recovery targets met

column4: Load test at hospital-wide volume
column5:
5,000 staff users and 1 million messages a day, from the design targets.

Acceptance criteria:
* Targets met with headroom

column4: Decide whether to split the API into separate services
column5:
The first release is one modular API on Container Apps. Split only where load or team ownership needs it.

Acceptance criteria:
* Decision recorded with measured evidence

column4: Monthly cloud cost review and budgets
column5:
Budget alerts by environment, and a monthly review.

Acceptance criteria:
* Budgets and alerts configured
* Review notes kept
